segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, um.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Right, I think everyone's here, so let's get started.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yep.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So, welcome to the first meeting, the kickoff meeting, for our new project.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: I'm Helen, I'll be the project manager on this one.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Um, maybe we can just go round and introduce ourselves quickly?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Sure, uh, I'm Marcus, I'm the industrial designer.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: So I'll be looking at, you know, the physical side, components, casing, that sort of thing.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: I'm Priya, marketing.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, so user research, trends, what sells.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And I'm Tom, I'm doing user interface.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Great.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay so the project. We're designing a kitchen timer.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: But a voice-controlled one.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Oh, so like you just say "timer, ten minutes" and—

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Exactly, yeah, hands-free.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: The idea is you've got flour on your hands or you're stirring something, you don't want to be pressing buttons.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Mm, that makes sense actually.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So, um, quickly the budget side.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Management want it selling at around twenty euros.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And production cost has to stay under ten euros a unit.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Under ten. Including the voice bit?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Including everything, yeah.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Hmm. Okay.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Um, and then the way this works, we've got four meetings: this one, functional design, conceptual design, and detailed design.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And between meetings you each work on your own bit and bring it back.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So, let's just pin down the next one now so it's in diaries.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: How about Thursday, two o'clock?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Thursday's fine for me.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, works.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, Thursday two, fine.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, Thursday at two then, functional design.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Right, so, first thoughts. Um, what do we think a kitchen timer like this needs to do?

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Well the obvious thing is setting a time by voice, and like cancelling it.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And maybe asking how much time is left.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: From what I've seen, people complain a lot about timers they can't hear, when the extractor fan's going and that.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So the alarm needs to be properly loud.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Well, and the same problem the other way, right, the microphone has to hear you over the fan.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, exactly.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: And people want it to understand them first time, any accent, from across the room.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Oh, perfect, so we're building a full smart speaker for ten euros. Easy.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Ha.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay, okay, I'm not saying all of it.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: No, we're definitely not building a smart speaker.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: But Marcus, seriously, is voice recognition even doable at that cost?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Um, I think so, if we keep it simple.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: There are cheap chips that only listen for a handful of fixed commands. They don't need internet.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: So not like, full speech, just maybe ten or twenty words.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: That's actually fine for a timer though.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Like, numbers, minutes, seconds, start, stop.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, that sounds sensible.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Would it still need a wake word? Like "hey timer"?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Probably, otherwise it's going off every time someone says "five" on the radio.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Right, yeah.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And I think we'd want at least one actual button. As a backup.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: In case it doesn't hear you, or someone just wants to shut the alarm up.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Everyone happy with that? Voice first but with a physical button.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Yeah, definitely.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, makes it easier to sell as well I'd think.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay, so, voice plus a backup button.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Oh, and what about running more than one timer at once? Like the pasta and the garlic bread.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Ooh, people would like that.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Hmm, that makes the commands more complicated though, you'd have to name them.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Let's park that one for the functional meeting, we can look at it properly then.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yeah, fair.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Um, okay.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So, the other thing for today is just getting used to the whiteboard, the drawing tool.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Could everyone just quickly draw their favourite animal? It's sort of the standard warm-up.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Oh god, um.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay this is meant to be a cat.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: It's... it's got six legs.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Those are whiskers!

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Oh. Okay.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Mine's a fish because fish are easy.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Very efficient.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Right, good, everyone's figured out the pens at least.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: So, jobs before the next meeting.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Marcus, can you look into the components? The voice chip, microphone, speaker, battery, what it'd cost roughly.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, I'll do that.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I'll see what the cheapest decent recognition module is.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Tom, can you work on the interaction side? So what the actual commands would be, and what it shows or says back.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Yep. I'll draft a command list.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And Priya, user requirements, what people want from kitchen timers, and what competitors are out there.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Sure. I'll look at what's already on the market.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: I might do a quick survey as well, like ten or so people who cook a lot.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Great, yeah.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: And I'll write up the minutes and send them round.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Oh, um, actually, sorry—

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I've just remembered I'm at the supplier on Thursday afternoon.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: The component people, so it's kind of useful for this, but I won't be back in time for two.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Ah. Okay. When could you do?

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Friday morning? Anytime Friday morning.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Priya, Tom, does Friday work?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Friday morning's okay. Not before ten though.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Friday's fine.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay so let's say Friday, ten o'clock, instead of Thursday.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Yeah, sorry about that.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: No, it's fine, and you'll have actual prices by then, so that's better anyway.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: True.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: I'll send a new invite with the minutes so nobody turns up Thursday.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: So, sorry, the survey, should I have results by Friday?

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Even a few responses would help, yeah.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: And are we thinking battery or plugged in? Because that kind of affects what I do with the display.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Not sure yet. Battery's nicer on a counter but the mic listening all the time drains it.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: I'll check that as part of the components.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Yeah, let's leave that open till Friday.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Anything else from anyone?

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Um, no, I think that's it.

segments.speaker: D
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: A
segments.text: Okay. So, Friday at ten, functional design. Thanks everyone.

segments.speaker: B
segments.text: Cheers.

segments.speaker: C
segments.text: Thanks.

abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, and the team members introduced themselves in their roles as project manager, industrial designer, marketing expert and user interface designer.

The project manager introduced the project, a hands-free voice-controlled kitchen timer with a target selling price of around 20 euros and a production cost under 10 euros per unit, and explained the four-meeting structure.

The team discussed initial requirements: an alarm loud enough to hear over an extractor fan, a microphone that can pick up the user over kitchen noise, and voice commands to set, cancel and query the timer.

The industrial designer said voice recognition is feasible within budget if a cheap offline chip recognising a small fixed set of commands is used, and the team agreed the timer should be voice-first with a physical backup button.

The team practised with the whiteboard drawing tool, assigned individual tasks, and scheduled the functional design meeting for Friday at 10:00, revised from an earlier plan of Thursday at 14:00 because the industrial designer has a supplier visit on Thursday afternoon.
actions: The industrial designer will research components (voice recognition chip, microphone, speaker, battery) and their approximate costs, including the cheapest adequate recognition module.
The industrial designer will investigate battery versus mains power, given the drain of an always-listening microphone.
The user interface designer will draft a voice command list and define what the timer displays or says back.
The marketing expert will research user requirements for kitchen timers and review competing products on the market.
The marketing expert will run a quick survey of around ten people who cook a lot, with early responses by the next meeting.
The project manager will write up and circulate the minutes along with a new invitation for the Friday 10:00 meeting.
decisions: The next meeting (functional design) will be held on Friday at 10:00; this replaces the earlier agreed Thursday 14:00 slot.
The timer will be primarily voice-controlled but will include at least one physical backup button.
Voice recognition will be kept simple, using a low-cost offline chip that recognises a small fixed set of commands.
problems: Whether the timer should support multiple simultaneous timers was parked for the functional design meeting, as it complicates the command set.
Whether a wake word is needed was raised but not settled.
Battery versus mains power is undecided and affects the display design.
Meeting the under-10-euro production cost with voice recognition, a loud alarm and a noise-robust microphone remains to be confirmed.
